request.spec:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.
request.prompt:

Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column

agent.result_text:
I added the column chooser, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

**What it does**
- The People section now has a "Columns" box with one checkbox per column, `column-<id>`. Each checkbox is ticked while its column is shown.
- The spec also switches off `person-excess`, which wasn't in the request's list, so I added an `excess` checkbox too. That makes 15 columns.
- A column you switch off has no cell at all, and its table heading goes with it. Totals, the summary, the page header and every figure are unchanged.

**Where it's kept**
The switched-off columns are kept in the screen's URL (a `hiddenColumns` parameter), the same way the app already keeps "show retired" and the sort order. So it's per screen: each signed-in user's browser has its own setting, and it stays as it is when another sheet is loaded. Nothing is stored on the server and nothing is written to the audit file, which matches what the spec expects. One catch: two people signing in one after the other on the same browser tab would share the setting.

**Things you might not expect**
- **Columns that share a cell:** statement count, stated total and statement date share one cell, which also holds the Statement buttons. Switching one off removes only that value, and the buttons stay. Overdue count and overdue total work the same way, and their cell and heading go only when both are off.
- **Columns whose cell holds controls:** Hold, Retired, Aliases and Patrons each have their own cell, which also holds that column's controls (for example the hold dates and Hold button). Switching one of these columns off hides its controls as well, so you can't hold or retire someone until the column is back on.

The new code is in `src/main/frontend/features/people/useColumns.tsx`. The rest of the change wraps the existing cells and headings so they can be switched off. I didn't run a separate TypeScript check because `tsc` isn't installed directly; the `bin/e2e` build went through.
